'''Leslie Frederick Greengard''' (born 1957) is an American [[mathematician]], [[physicist]] and [[computer scientist]].<ref name="ams_notices_2001">{{cite journal|url=https://www.ams.org/notices/200104/comm-steele.pdf|title=2001 Steele Prizes|journal=[[Notices of the American Mathematical Society]]|volume=48|issue=4|pages=404–407|date={{Format date|2001|04}}|accessdate={{Format date|2010|12|21}}}}</ref><ref name="CV_NSSEFF">{{cite news|url=http://nsseff.ida.org/pages/cvs/Greengard-CV.pdf|title=Current NSSEFF Fellows - 2010 Fellows|publisher=[[U.S. Department of Defense]]|accessdate={{Format date|2011|3|11}}|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20110726171359/http://nsseff.ida.org/pages/cvs/Greengard-CV.pdf|archivedate=2011-07-26}}</ref> He is co-inventor with [[Vladimir Rokhlin Jr.]] of the [[fast multipole method]] (FMM) in 1987, recognized as one of the top-ten [[algorithms]] of the 20th century.<ref name="ams_notices_2001"/><ref>{{cite journal|first=Barry Arthur|last=Cipra|authorlink=Barry Arthur Cipra|date=May 16, 2000|title=The Best of the 20th Century: Editors Name Top 10 Algorithms|journal=SIAM News|volume=33|issue=4|page=2|publisher=Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics|url=http://www.siam.org/news/news.php?id=637|accessdate={{Format date|2011|2|16}}|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110615092015/http://www.siam.org/news/news.php?id=637|archive-date=June 15, 2011|url-status=dead|df=mdy-all}}</ref>

Greengard was elected as a member of the [[National Academy of Engineering]] in 2006 for work on the development of algorithms and software for fast multipole methods.

==Short biography==
Leslie Frederick Greengard<ref name="thesis">{{cite thesis |last=Greengard |first=Leslie Frederick |date=1987 |title=The Rapid Evaluation of Potential Fields in Particle Systems |url= |type=PhD |chapter= |publisher=[[Yale University]] |docket= |oclc= |access-date=}}</ref> was born in 1957 in [[London, England]],<ref name="ieee">{{cite web |title=IEEE Author: Leslie Greengard |url=https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/author/38550912100 |website=[[IEEE]] |access-date=March 19, 2022}}</ref> but grew up in the [[United States]] in [[New York City]], [[Boston]], and [[New Haven]]. He holds a B.A. in [[mathematics]] from [[Wesleyan University]] (1979), an M.D. from the [[Yale School of Medicine]] (1987), and a Ph.D. in [[computer science]] from [[Yale University]] (1987).<ref name="ams_notices_2001"/><ref name="CV_NSSEFF"/>

From 2006 to 2011, Greengard was director of the [[Courant Institute of Mathematical Sciences]], an independent division of the [[New York University]] (NYU)<ref name="CV_NSSEFF"/><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.nyu.edu/about/news-publications/news/2006/04/26/nyu_names_mathematician_leslie.html|title=NYU Names Mathematician Leslie Greengard As Director of Courant Institute of Mathematical Sciences|author=John Beckman|newspaper=NYU Today|publisher=[[New York University]]|date={{Format date|2006|4|26}} |accessdate={{Format date|2011|3|11}}}}</ref> and is currently a professor of [[mathematics]] and [[computer science]] at Courant. He is also a professor at [[New York University Tandon School of Engineering]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.poly.edu/academics/departments/electrical/people|title = Home &#124; NYU Tandon School of Engineering}}</ref> and the director of the Simons Center for Data Analysis.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.simonsfoundation.org/simons-center-for-data-analysis/scda-staff |title=SCDA Staff &#124; Simons Foundation |access-date=2015-11-16 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151117110929/https://www.simonsfoundation.org/simons-center-for-data-analysis/scda-staff/ |archive-date=2015-11-17 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

He formerly served as the Director at the Center for Computational Biology at the [[Flatiron Institute]]. {{As of|2018|10}}, he has assumed the directorship of the new Center of Computational Mathematics at the Institute.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.simonsfoundation.org/2018/10/01/ccm-launch/|title = Flatiron Institute Launches Center for Computational Mathematics|date = October 2018}}</ref>

He is the son of neuroscientist [[Paul Greengard]] and the nephew of Irene Kane, later known as [[Chris Chase]], an actress, writer, and journalist.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://articles.nydailynews.com/2003-02-03/news/18218126_1_gifted-kids-josephine-baker-role-models|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120515225133/http://articles.nydailynews.com/2003-02-03/news/18218126_1_gifted-kids-josephine-baker-role-models|url-status=dead|archive-date=May 15, 2012|title=A Nobel Patriarch 2000 Winner Head Of Talented Family|author=Clem Richardson|newspaper=NYDailyNews.com|publisher=[[Daily News (New York)|Daily News]]|date={{Format date|2003|2|3}}|accessdate={{Format date|2011|5|31}}}}</ref>

==Awards and honors==
* 2016, fellow of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]]<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.amacad.org/content/members/newFellows.aspx?s=c|title=Newly Elected Members|date=April 2016|publisher=[[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]]|access-date=2016-04-20}}</ref>
* 2014, [https://www.siam.org/prizes/sponsored/vonneumann.php Von Neumann Lecture], [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]]
* 2011, [[Wilbur Cross Medal]]
* 2010, Plenary Speaker, SIAM Annual Meeting
* 2010, "National Security Science and Engineering Faculty Fellowship", from the [[U.S. Department of Defense]] (DoD)<ref>{{cite web |url=http://nsseff.ida.org/pages/fellows.html |title=Current NSSEFF Fellows - 2010 Fellows |publisher=[[U.S. Department of Defense]] |access-date={{Format date|2011|3|11}} |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://archive.today/20110726170444/http://nsseff.ida.org/pages/fellows.html |archivedate=2011-07-26 }}</ref>
* 2006, elected to the [[United States National Academy of Engineering|U.S. National Academy of Engineering]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nae.edu/MembersSection/Directory20412/30170.aspx|title=NAE Members Directory - Dr. Leslie Greengard |publisher=U.S. National Academy of Engineering|access-date={{Format date|2011|2|16}}}}</ref>
* 2006, elected to the [[United States National Academy of Sciences|U.S. National Academy of Sciences]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nasonline.org/site/Dir?sid=1011&view=basic&pg=srch|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20051025074536/http://www.nasonline.org/site/Dir?sid=1011&view=basic&pg=srch|url-status=dead|archive-date=October 25, 2005|title=NAS Membership Directory |publisher=U.S. National Academy of Sciences|access-date={{Format date|2011|2|20}}}}</ref>
* 2005, Plenary Speaker, 2nd National Congress on Applied and Industrial Mathematics (France)
* 2004, "Margaret and Herman Sokol Faculty Award in the Sciences" from the [[New York University]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://as.nyu.edu/object/aboutas.honorsawards.0405|title=Arts & Science - 2004-2005 Faculty Honors and Awards|publisher=[[New York University]]|access-date={{Format date|2011|3|11}}|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110720014700/http://as.nyu.edu/object/aboutas.honorsawards.0405|archive-date=2011-07-20|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cims.nyu.edu/events/archive/fall_04.html|title=Events - Previous Weekly Bulletins|publisher=[[Courant Institute of Mathematical Sciences]]|date={{Format date|2004|11|16}}|accessdate={{Format date|2011|3|11}}}}</ref>
* 2001, [[Leroy P. Steele Prize for Seminal Contribution to Research]] from the [[American Mathematical Society]] (together with [[Vladimir Rokhlin (American scientist)|Vladimir Rokhlin]]), for their paper describing a new algorithm: the [[fast multipole method]] (FMM)<ref name="ams_notices_2001"/>
* 2000, Plenary Speaker, SIAM Conference on Computational Science & Engineering
* 1999, Plenary Speaker, International Congress on Industrial and Applied Mathematics
* 1998, Invited Speaker, International Congress of Mathematicians<ref>{{cite book|author=Greengard, Leslie|author2=Sun, Xiaobai|chapter=A new version of the fast Gauss transform|title=Doc. Math. (Bielefeld) Extra Vol. ICM Berlin, 1998, vol. III|year=1998|pages=575–584|chapter-url=https://www.elibm.org/ft/10011612000}}</ref>
* 1990, "Fellowship for Science and Engineering" from the [[Packard Foundation]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.packard.org/genericDetails.aspx?RootCatID=3&CategoryID=152 |title=Fellowship for Science and Engineering |publisher=[[David and Lucile Packard Foundation]] |access-date={{Format date|2011|2|19}} |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20110211121102/http://www.packard.org/genericDetails.aspx?RootCatID=3&CategoryID=152 |archivedate=2011-02-11 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.packard.org/fellowsDetails.aspx?RootCatID=3&CategoryID=70&ItemID=2637|title=Fellowship for Science and Engineering - Leslie F. Greengard|publisher=[[David and Lucile Packard Foundation]]|access-date={{Format date|2011|2|19}}}}{{dead link|date=December 2017 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>
* 1990, [[Presidential Young Investigator Award]] from the [[National Science Foundation]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nsf.gov/awardsearch/showAward.do?AwardNumber=9058579|title=Presidential Young Investigator Award: Rapid Numerical Algorithms for Scientific Computation|publisher=[[National Science Foundation]] |access-date={{Format date|2011|2|19}}}}</ref>
* 1987–1989, "Mathematical Sciences Postdoctoral Research Fellowship" from the [[National Science Foundation]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nsf.gov/awardsearch/showAward.do?AwardNumber=8705793|title=Mathematical Sciences Postdoctoral Research Fellowship|publisher=[[National Science Foundation]]|access-date={{Format date|2011|2|20}}}}</ref>
* 1987, [[Council of Graduate Schools]]/[[University Microfilms International]] Distinguished Dissertation Award, for his PhD. [[dissertation]] "The Rapid Evaluation of Potential Fields in Particle Systems"<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cgsnet.org/Default.aspx?tabid=131|title=Awards - CGS/UMI Distinguished Dissertation|publisher=[[Council of Graduate Schools]]|access-date={{Format date|2011|2|20}}|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20110128155818/http://www.cgsnet.org/Default.aspx?tabid=131|archivedate=2011-01-28}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.proquest.com/en-US/promos/hos/feature11_hos_ph.shtml|title=Hall of Scholars: past winners of the CGS/UMI Distinguished Dissertation Award|access-date={{Format date|2011|2|20}}|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20101205200154/http://www.proquest.com/en-US/promos/hos/feature11_hos_ph.shtml|archivedate=2010-12-05|id={{ProQuest|}}}}</ref>
* 1987, "Doctoral Dissertation Award", Series Winner from the [[Association for Computing Machinery]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://awards.acm.org/doctoral_dissertation|title=Doctoral Dissertation Award |publisher=[[Association for Computing Machinery]]|access-date={{Format date|2011|2|20}}}}</ref>
* 1987, Sandoz Thesis Award from the [[Yale School of Medicine]]
* 1979–1986, [[Public Health Service]] – National Research Service Award [[Medical Scientist Training Program]]
